source: Brazilian E-Commerce Public Dataset by Olist, 2016–2018
grain: One delivered order per row, with usable delivery and estimated dates

table_grains.delivery_summary.csv: One row per delivery status; no duplicate overall row
table_grains.delay_buckets.csv: One row per non-overlapping delay bucket
table_grains.monthly_delivery.csv: One row per observed purchase month, including tiny cohorts
table_grains.state_delivery.csv: One row per customer state; all states retained
table_grains.daily_delay_reviews.csv: One row per observed signed calendar-day delay; no display-range truncation

methods.late: Delivered calendar date after estimated calendar date; same-day deliveries are on time
methods.reviews: Mean score among reviewed orders only; missing scores are excluded, not treated as zero
methods.duplicate_reviews: The SQL fact export selects the latest answered review to preserve order grain
methods.denominators: Rates use delivered-order counts; review means use reviewed-order counts; late-delay mean uses late-order count
methods.numeric_precision: CSV ratios and means are rounded to eight decimals; JSON retains full floating-point precision; counts and sums are exact integers

limits: Delivery/rating differences are descriptive associations, not proof of causation or intervention impact.
Only eligible delivered orders are included; canceled, undelivered and missing-date orders can have different review patterns.
Small cohorts can produce volatile rates; inspect order and reviewed-order counts before interpreting rankings.
Historical Brazilian public data do not establish current business performance.

seller_source.attribution: One distinct order per participating seller; a multi-seller order can count for multiple sellers.
